title: Update on FDA's ongoing evaluation of reports of suicidal thoughts or actions in patients taking a certain type of medicines approved for type 2 diabetes and obesity
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Safety Communication, 11 January 2024
result: The preliminary evaluation found no evidence that GLP-1 receptor agonists cause suicidal thoughts or actions. FAERS reports were often limited and influenced by other factors and did not demonstrate a clear relationship; reviews of clinical trials, including large outcome studies, and of observational studies found no association. Because few suicidal thoughts or actions occurred in both treated and control groups, FDA stated it could not definitively rule out a small risk and planned a meta-analysis of trials across all GLP-1 receptor agonists and a Sentinel analysis. The suicidality information then in the labels of GLP-1 receptor agonists for weight management was described as based on reports with a variety of older weight-loss medicines. The page, archived on 11 March 2026, carries a notice of a further FDA Drug Safety Communication issued on 13 January 2026.
